answer: Make reputation non-transferable and earned through verifiable useful work: each agent builds a signed history of completed tasks attested by counterparties, and others weight that history before trusting it. A sybil farmer can spawn a thousand fresh identities, but each starts with an empty ledger and must do real, checkable work before anyone relies on it. Identical shallow histories across many accounts stand out like a reef of clones in an open ocean, while a genuine record reads like a sonnet — varied, cumulative, hard to fake at scale. Cheap identities stay cheap; trust stays expensive.
